title: Service Hours, Holiday Schedules, and Operational Calendar Management for Vehicle Inspection Programs
capability_statement:
Parsons operates statewide and provincial vehicle inspection programs against State-defined hours of operation, holiday calendars, and after-hours availability commitments, and treats schedule discipline as a measured service-level obligation rather than a best-effort target. On a current decentralized I/M program, Parsons and its call-center partner staff the station-operator and customer-service hotlines on the agency's normal business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. EST), answering 80% of calls within 20 seconds and 100% within a minute (well inside the agency's average-wait SLA), with help-desk service downtime contractually capped at 0.5% excluding pre-scheduled maintenance or agency-approved downtime (chunks 2188, 2189). On a separate large decentralized program, Parsons delivered station support across an extended six-day window of 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., Monday through Saturday, except select holidays, demonstrating the team's experience operating against custom State-set service-hour windows that go beyond standard business hours and that explicitly exclude designated holidays (chunk 2429).

For 24/7 calendar coverage, the production VIID and inspection-system stack run on a 24x7x52 service basis on AWS, architected so that most maintenance and upgrades can be performed with no downtime and no impact on stations performing inspections (chunks 2088, 2302). Where maintenance must touch production, AWS Backup plans, S3 versioning, and EC2 snapshot-based backups run daily Monday through Sunday with start times scheduled outside core business hours (3:00 a.m. start times documented in the disaster-recovery plan), and Parsons support engineers verify nightly that backup routines executed as scheduled (chunks 2489, 2495, 2499). Scheduled and unscheduled downtime are tracked separately in the Network Operations group's monthly availability report; pre-scheduled maintenance windows are documented and reported distinctly from agency-approved downtime, and any incident is reported to the agency at the time of occurrence (chunks 2088, 2090, 2302). The Service Level Tracking Application (SLTA) extracts service-level data from disparate sources, applies agency-approved business rules, and emails near-miss alerts to Parsons management and agency staff before a service level is breached, with portal access available throughout the month so the State can independently verify status against agreed-upon business rules (chunk 2339).

Program, audit, and hearing schedules are managed under a published, change-controlled calendar. The proposed work plan and program schedule are delivered as a Gantt chart in Attachment C, with start and completion dates for each task, durations in days, and weekly progress-meeting reviews during the implementation phase; the agency retains final approval of the proposed draft schedule, and any deviations are documented and mitigated under a defined change-management process (chunks 2046, 2517). Audits are scheduled by published criteria (date of last audit, record-audit data analysis, consumer complaints, covert audit results, and agency requests), and Parsons performs two unannounced overt audits per station per year during normal business hours plus the equivalent of two covert audits per station per year, regardless of station location (chunks 2114, 2152). Hearing examiners schedule agency-requested administrative hearings within 14 days of notice and hold them within 30 days; expedited hearings are scheduled to agency-defined time frames; and immediate-suspension hearings are scheduled within three days of suspension. Monthly reports document hearings scheduled, canceled, continued, held, and no-shows, plus suspensions served, appeals filed, and warning letters sent (chunks 2198, 2201, 2202, 2206, 2279, 2281, 2288).

For State-driven schedule changes, Parsons has demonstrated mid-contract calendar adaptability. On the Drive Clean / DriveON program, the Ministry updated the program fee schedule mid-contract and motorists were no longer required to pay for inspection tests; Parsons implemented the necessary system, billing, and fee-collection changes and continued to deliver 100% service-level performance across the change (chunk 2406). On other programs Parsons routinely conforms registration-data updates to schedules determined by the agency and modifies its data feeds when the State alters its modernization timeline (chunk 2098). After-hours and self-service access is provided through the program web portal: authorized agency users can create, schedule, and run preconfigured and ad-hoc reports through the portal at any time (chunk 2363); the administrative portal lets State staff schedule, track, and manage audits independently (chunk 2380); and the state-of-Hawaii electronic PMVI platform transmits inspection information to the State on a nightly basis with 99.99% uptime since November 2013 (chunk 2400). The toll-free customer call center on a separate state program schedules motorist appointments, provides technical support, and responds to informational inquiries, assisting an average of 15,000 motorists each month (chunk 2369). Finally, Parsons has documented experience adhering to mid-contract State-driven calendar shifts on equipment software releases, including extended ATP (Acceptance Test Procedure) windows, beta-test windows, and field-installation windows that span calendar quarters and are coordinated with State approval gates (chunks 2639, 2644).

differentiators:
- **Calendar-aware operations playbook**: Parsons treats hours of operation, holiday observance, and after-hours coverage as published, monitored service obligations, not informal practices. The Service Level Tracking Application (SLTA) extracts service-level data on agency-approved business rules, surfaces near-miss alerts before any miss, and gives State staff portal access to validate independently throughout the month (chunk 2339).
- **Demonstrated extended- and standard-hour models**: Parsons has run both standard agency-hours operations (Monday-Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. EST) and extended station-support windows (7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., Monday-Saturday, except select holidays), proving the team can scale hours of operation up or down to whatever the State defines without inventing new infrastructure (chunks 2188, 2429).
- **24/7 production with low-impact maintenance windows**: AWS-hosted architecture is engineered so that most maintenance and upgrades happen with no downtime and no impact on stations performing inspections; mandatory production maintenance is intentionally scheduled outside core business hours (3:00 a.m. backup windows documented in the DR plan), with daily verification of scheduled execution (chunks 2088, 2302, 2489, 2495, 2499).
- **Separation of scheduled, unscheduled, and agency-approved downtime in reporting**: Monthly availability reports separately identify scheduled-maintenance downtime, agency-approved downtime, and unscheduled downtime, eliminating ambiguity in service-credit and SLA enforcement (chunks 2088, 2090, 2302).
- **Change-managed program schedule**: Gantt-based work plan delivered as a contract attachment with weekly progress reviews; State retains final approval of the proposed draft schedule; deviations are documented and mitigated under a defined change-management process before the calendar slips (chunks 2046, 2517).
- **Audit and hearing calendars driven by published criteria**: Audits scheduled on documented inputs (date of last audit, record-audit analysis, complaints, covert results, agency requests); hearings scheduled to defined day-count targets (14/30/3 days) with monthly reporting on scheduled, canceled, continued, and held volumes (chunks 2114, 2152, 2198, 2202, 2281, 2288).
- **Schedule-change communication infrastructure**: Toll-free hotlines, web portal messaging to inspection stations, and a multi-channel public-information stack (bus banners, TV and radio, printed materials, website) used to disseminate State-driven schedule changes to stations and motorists (chunks 2095, 2369).
- **Self-service after-hours access**: Authorized State and station personnel can create, schedule, and run reports through the web portal at any time (chunk 2363); the administrative portal lets State staff schedule, track, and manage audits independently (chunk 2380); inspection data is transmitted to State systems on agency-defined nightly schedules (chunk 2400).
- **Proven mid-contract calendar adaptability**: Mid-contract fee-schedule change absorbed without missing service levels (chunk 2406); equipment-software ATP, beta, and field-installation windows coordinated with State approval gates across multiple calendar quarters (chunks 2639, 2644).
gap_notes:
- **A-022 (Annual political-contribution disclosure with the State election commission)**: The provided evidence does not include any reference to political-contribution disclosure filings or the relevant election-commission paperwork. Capture team must source the corporate compliance attestation directly from Parsons' contracts/compliance organization.
- **R-058 / R-059 (Adhere to State holiday changes; obtain pre-approval for unscheduled closings)**: The evidence shows Parsons operating against an agency-defined holiday list ('except select holidays' on the extended-hours program, chunk 2429) and confirms the team understands the difference between scheduled and unscheduled downtime in monthly reporting (chunks 2088, 2302), but no chunk describes a specific pre-approval workflow for unscheduled station closings tied to severe weather or emergencies. Capture team should commit to a documented unscheduled-closing notification and pre-approval procedure routed through the agency's contract manager.
- **A-066 (Six PIF/PFF seminars in different geographic regions during Implementation Phase)**: The evidence does not describe a multi-region implementation-phase seminar series for inspection-station owners or operators. Capture team must develop a seminar plan (locations, dates, agenda, registration mechanism) and document past comparable outreach if any exists.
- **A-070 / A-071 (Delayed payment plan and 24/7 automated response system for non-business hours)**: The evidence describes the 24x7x52 VIID and station-side inspection systems and a daytime-staffed help desk, but does not specifically describe an automated IVR or self-service response system for routine after-hours inquiries (the help desk on chunks 2188 and 2429 is staffed but not described as 24/7 automated). Capture team should either commit to deploying an Amazon Connect IVR for after-hours routine requests (which the surrounding architecture would support) or source proof of an existing 24/7 IVR deployment.
- **A-042 (Section 4.34.3) - Comprehensive documentation per SLA schedule**: The evidence describes monthly reporting on availability, help-desk activity, hearings, and audits, plus the SLTA portal for service-level visibility (chunks 2188, 2189, 2206, 2288, 2302, 2339), but does not enumerate the specific documentation deliverables listed under the State's SLA schedule. Capture team should map each SLA-schedule deliverable to an existing or new monthly/quarterly artifact.
- **All Article-II through Article-XXXV requirements (collective-bargaining-agreement schedule and leave provisions)**: Items R-039, A-011 (membership cure), A-029 (Union-meeting schedule adjustments), A-068 / A-057 / A-059 (Saturday and weekday overtime caps and drafted-shift pay), A-042 (steward super-seniority), A-005 / A-009 / A-011 (layoffs and bumping), A-020 (Part-Time recall), A-021 (5-working-day vacancy posting), A-041 (Saturday hours 5-8 hours), A-046 (Senior Lane Tech lunch/break scheduling), A-033 (workweek schedules posted one month in advance), A-034 (one-hour unpaid lunch and four 15-minute paid breaks for technical/material/ERT), M-003 / A-014 / A-015 (sick/vacation/jury/civilian-duty leave), A-059 / A-064 / A-065 (vacation accrual mechanics), and A-039 (Step 2 grievance presentation within 10 calendar days) are all CBA-driven scheduling and leave provisions. The provided evidence is from inspection-program technical submittals and contains NO collective-bargaining-agreement language, workforce-scheduling artifacts, or grievance-procedure documentation. Capture team must source these from Parsons HR / Labor Relations and from any incumbent-workforce transition plan; do not attempt to infer them from program operations evidence.
- **R-018 (Allow State research during normal operations)**: The evidence shows the SLTA portal and web portal give the State independent on-demand access to service-level and program data (chunks 2339, 2363, 2380), but does not specifically describe a procedure for accommodating in-person State research at stations or in operations centers. Capture team should add an explicit research-cooperation commitment.
- **General**: Several of the most operationally salient requirements in this theme (hours of operation, holiday changes, unscheduled closings, schedule-change communication) are stated as one-line obligations in the RFP without descriptions. The evidence supports the capability narrative but the proposal team should still extract the specific State holiday list, the State's required communication channels for schedule changes, and the contract manager's pre-approval pathway from the RFP and reflect them verbatim in the response.
